reasoning: Both are jazz-trained musicians whose defining move was refusing to stay inside jazz — and both used hip-hop as the exit door. BBNG covered Odd Future and MF DOOM before they had an original album. Washington played on To Pimp a Butterfly before The Epic came out. The hip-hop world didn't dilute their jazz — it clarified what they actually wanted to do with it. The divergence is instructive: BBNG moved toward restraint and orchestral intimacy (Talk Memory), Washington moved toward expansiveness and spiritual grandeur (The Epic). Same room, different corners. Both treat jazz as a living language rather than a museum piece, and both arrived at that position through the same unlikely route.
